answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies rests on bonding with slashing. Each new agent posts a bond, and the protocol samples the population on an unpredictable pulse; anyone caught running duplicate identities forfeits the whole bond. The stake exceeds what one identity earns before detection, so N fake agents need N frozen stakes. Cost scales linearly with clones while revenue does not, making the assault unprofitable. Since the bond attaches to a verified island of evidence, not a name, cheap aliases cannot dodge it: honest agents pay once, while every cedar touch by a faker burns capital.
